_meta.source: TT13 Fantasy League Bylaws (Google Doc, modified 2025-08-19)
_meta.note: Every field carries a `confidence` marker. 'stated' = written verbatim in the bylaws. 'inferred' = reconstructed from cross-referencing, tallies reconcile exactly but needs commissioner confirmation. 'unknown' = not in the source, must be filled by hand or by API ingest. NOTHING here is invented.
_meta.seasonConvention: seasonYear = the calendar year the NFL season begins. '24-'25 in the bylaws == seasonYear 2024.

league.name: TT13's Fantasy Challenge

platformHistory.note: Foley's champion declaration for '25-'26: 'Changes platform to Sleeper to support this change.'

scoringHistory.note: Foley's declaration. Positional-differential PPR is why the league left Yahoo.

league.goldenRule: No slouching on your team. Zero tolerance for late-season automatic bye weeks due to negligence.
league.championPerk: The champion may add or subtract one rule — roster positions, scoring settings, or a fun rule to modernize the league. Recorded as a Champion's Declaration.
league.championPerkSecond: The champion also NAMES the following chapter. Binh won Chapter IV and named Chapter V 'The Flemish Giant Invitational' after his own team. This also resolves the Drive doc titled 'The Flemish Giant Invitational Fantasy Football League Constitutional Bylaws' — it is the Chapter V rulebook, not a separate league.
league.ringInspirationRule: Each chapter's ring is modeled on the Super Bowl champion of ITS OWN NFL season. A fantasy season played Sept–Dec of year Y ends in January of Y+1; that same NFL season's Super Bowl is played weeks later in February of Y+1, and its real ring is unveiled the following summer. So the ring is struck and UNVEILED at the kickoff of the next fantasy season, once its real-world inspiration exists. Chapter VII (NFL 2026) therefore has no ring yet — Super Bowl LXI has not been played.

managers.name: Jake Kaufman
managers.note: 5 playoff appearances in 5 years, zero finals. The league's defining hard-luck story — worth its own Hall of Records callout.

managers.name: Binh Nguyen
managers.note: Only two-time champion in league history. Most decorated manager.

managers.name: Timmy Nguyen
managers.note: Did not play 2024; returned for 2025, reclaiming Pat's slot.

managers.name: Pat
managers.note: Finished 9th in '24–'25 and left the league. Timmy Nguyen took back the slot for '25–'26.

championsDeclaration.note: No rule change — Binh declined to use the perk.

championsDeclaration.rule: Lowest-scoring team each week throws $5 into a pool, collected by the highest scoring team at season's end.

seasons._note: Maniel won as a first-year manager.

championsDeclaration.rule: $5 penalty goes directly to that week's high scorer instead of pooling. Lowest-scoring team must record 10 push-ups and send to chat.

seasons._note: Flemish Giant is Binh's team name and is used for both of his titles (2020 and 2023).

championsDeclaration.rule: Removes the $5 punishment, keeps the 10 push-ups. Scoring becomes 0.5 PPR receivers / 1.0 RB / 1.5 TE. Moves the league to Sleeper to support it.

storylines: Foley won the title at 6-8 — a losing regular season. The lowest-seeded champion in league history.
Maniel finished 11-3, the best record in the league, and placed 5th.
Binh, the two-time champion, finished 11th at 5-9.
Holmqvist won it all in his second season, one year after finishing 12th at 4-10 as a rookie. Worst to first.
seasons._gap: Full standings and records are on Sleeper and pullable from the open API with no application required — the fastest real data available.
